snippets: Gukesh Sindarov Geneva draw 2026 FIDE World Chess Championship updates. Follow Bhaskar English. Indian Grandmaster D Gukesh drew with Uzbekistans Javokhir Sindarov in the second game of the 2026 FIDE World Chess Championship on Wednesday. The match was played in Geneva, with Gukesh playing with the white pieces.

Indian Grandmaster D Gukesh drew with Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in the second game of the 2026 FIDE World Chess Championship on Wednesday. The match was played in Geneva, with Gukesh playing with the white pieces. The game ended in a draw after 20 moves. Sindarov claimed a draw on the grounds that the same position had occurred three consecutive times. The second game of the championship therefore also ended without a result.

During the game, Gukesh fell behind Sindarov on the clock. At one point, he was around 35 minutes behind. He had also taken considerable time on the 15th move. However, the two players did not have to wait long for the game to produce a result.
In the game, Gukesh moved his pawn to F3 on the 15th move.
fCSuSmbz.title: Gukesh Sindarov Draw | Geneva FIDE World Chess Championship 2026

Written by Yannick Pelletier Photos: Michal Walusza The Salesforce FIDE World Championship Match 2026 is taking place at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, near Geneva, Switzerland, from November 22 to December 12.

Javokhir Sindarov and Gukesh Dommaraju drew their first encounter in the Salesforce FIDE World Championship Match 2026 in Geneva. Both players produced a highly accurate performance in a complex game, with neither managing to tilt the balance decisively in their favour.

A solid and well-fought opening encounter, with the match score now standing at 0.5–0.5. zGi5NE5i.description: Once again, Gukesh fell behind on the clock, but just when Sindarov had gone for a bold pawn push and action seemed to be heating up, the game ended in a 20-move draw by repetition, leaving the scores level at 1-1.
snippets: Gukesh, asked if he'd have preferred to win one of the first two games, quipped, "I’d have preferred both results go my way!" drawing the biggest smile from both players of the post-game interrogation. Gukesh was in good spirits in the post-game press conference. Photo: Michal Walusza/FIDE. He added, "I feel energetic on the board," and added, "away from the board I’ve been much happier here compared to Singapore." He put that down to the company of his two friends Charmie Kapoor and Shikhar Saxena. Gukesh brought two friends with him to Geneva and says he's "become a little more relaxed" than he was when he won the world championship title in Singapore.

World Champion Gukesh Dommaraju played the London System in game two of the Salesforce FIDE World Championship 2026, but Challenger GM Javokhir Sindarov was ready. Once again, Gukesh fell behind on the clock, but just when Sindarov had gone for a bold pawn push and action seemed to be heating up, the game ended in a 20-move draw by repetition, leaving the scores level at 1-1.

You can watch the Salesforce FIDE World Championship 2026 live on Chess.com/Events, Chess.com/TV and on the Chess.com Twitch and YouTube channels, while GM Hikaru Nakamura is streaming on Kick. The live broadcast is hosted by GMs Judit Polgar and David Howell. Check out Nakamura's recap of the game, as well as our full playlist with recaps by partner streamers, including IM Levy Rozman. GM Dejan Bojkov has annotated the game below. ... Game two of the match in Geneva was the first time Sindarov would get the black pieces in a world championship game.

The Salesforce FIDE World Championship 2026 in Geneva, Switzerland decides the next world champion. Uzbek Challenger Javokhir Sindarov plays Indian Defending Champion Gukesh Dommaraju in a 14-game match, with the winner the first to 7.5 points. The players have two hours for 40 moves, then 30 minutes to the end of the game, with 30 seconds added each move from move 41 onward.
zGi5NE5i.title: FIDE World Championship 2026 Game 2: London System Battle Ends In 20-Move Draw - Chess.com

snippets: The World Chess Championship match is taking place in Collonge, a suburb of Geneva, from November 24 to December 12, 2026. The format allows for up to 14 classical games, with the first player to score 7.5 points declared the winner.
